Nouragues H-D — Tropical Tree Height-Diameter Data, French Guiana

plant_scaling_data project

2026-05-02

1 Overview

NouraguesHD is a paired height-diameter dataset for tropical trees in the Nouragues Natural Reserve, French Guiana. It is distributed as part of the BIOMASS R package (Réjou-Méchain et al. 2017) and is used as a reference dataset for fitting local height-diameter models in tropical forest AGB estimation workflows.

The Nouragues Reserve is a pristine, undisturbed lowland tropical moist forest in central French Guiana (~4°N, 52–53°W), with no recent logging or major anthropogenic disturbance.

BIOMASS R package (data source): Réjou-Méchain M, Tanguy A, Piponiot C, Chave J, Hérault B (2017). BIOMASS: an R Package for estimating aboveground biomass and its uncertainty in tropical forests. Methods in Ecology and Evolution 8:1163–1167. doi: 10.1111/2041-210X.12753

Original Nouragues data (primary source): Coomes DA, Dalponte M, Jucker T, et al. (2017) Area-based vs tree-centric approaches to mapping forest carbon in Southeast Asian forests from airborne laser scanning data. Remote Sensing of Environment 194:77–88. (NouraguesHD is compiled from multiple field campaigns at this site.)

⚠ Citation note: The primary literature citation for the NouraguesHD dataset within the BIOMASS package should be verified — the package documentation credits Réjou-Méchain et al. (2017) as the package reference but does not provide a separate DOI for the dataset itself. The field measurements originate from the Nouragues long-term research station.

3 Geographic context

world <- map_data("world")

# Exact plot coordinates from data
plot_coords <- dat |>
  distinct(plotId, lat, long)

ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = world,
               aes(x = long, y = lat, group = group),
               fill = "grey88", color = "grey70", linewidth = 0.2) +
  geom_point(data = plot_coords,
             aes(x = long, y = lat, color = plotId),
             size = 6, alpha = 0.9) +
  geom_text(data = plot_coords,
            aes(x = long, y = lat, label = plotId),
            vjust = -1.2, size = 4, fontface = "bold") +
  coord_fixed(1.3, xlim = c(-65, -45), ylim = c(-5, 15)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Plot1 = "#d73027", Plot2 = "#4575b4")) +
  labs(
    title = "Nouragues H-D \u2014 exact plot locations in French Guiana",
    subtitle = paste0("Plot 1: ", round(plot_coords$lat[1],3), "\u00b0N, ",
                      round(plot_coords$long[1],3), "\u00b0E   |   ",
                      "Plot 2: ", round(plot_coords$lat[2],3), "\u00b0N, ",
                      round(plot_coords$long[2],3), "\u00b0E"),
    x = NULL, y = NULL, color = "Plot"
  ) +
  theme(axis.text = element_blank(), axis.ticks = element_blank(),
        panel.grid = element_blank())

Both plots are within the Nouragues Natural Reserve, separated by approximately 1.6 km based on their coordinate distances.

163 trees (15.5%) have no height measurement. Height was not measured for every tree in the field campaign. Missing heights must be imputed using the H~D model when computing AGB via the Chave et al. (2014) pantropical equation.

7 Height ~ DBH scaling

dat_hd <- dat |> filter(!is.na(H), D > 0, H > 0)

# Per-plot OLS log-log
models <- dat_hd |>
  group_by(plotId) |>
  summarise(
    n    = n(),
    beta = round(coef(lm(log(H) ~ log(D)))[2], 3),
    R2   = round(summary(lm(log(H) ~ log(D)))$r.squared, 3),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

ggplot(dat_hd, aes(x = D, y = H, color = plotId)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.5, size = 1.8) +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", formula = y ~ x,
              se = TRUE, linewidth = 1.2) +
  scale_x_log10(labels = comma, breaks = c(10, 20, 50, 100, 160)) +
  scale_y_log10(labels = comma, breaks = c(5, 10, 20, 40)) +

7.1 Weibull and Michaelis-Menten models (as used in BIOMASS)

# Fit the models used in BIOMASS::modelHD
dat_fit <- dat |> filter(!is.na(H), D > 0, H > 0)

# Weibull 3-parameter: H = a(1 - exp(-b*D^c))
weib_fit <- nls(H ~ a * (1 - exp(-b * D^c)),
                data = dat_fit,
                start = list(a = 50, b = 0.05, c = 0.7),
                control = nls.control(maxiter = 200))

# Michaelis-Menten: H = (a*D)/(b+D)
mm_fit   <- nls(H ~ (a * D) / (b + D),
                data = dat_fit,
                start = list(a = 60, b = 20),
                control = nls.control(maxiter = 200))

dbh_seq <- seq(min(dat_fit$D), max(dat_fit$D), length.out = 200)

pred_df <- data.frame(
  D     = dbh_seq,
  Weibull        = predict(weib_fit, newdata = data.frame(D = dbh_seq)),
  Michaelis_Menten = predict(mm_fit, newdata = data.frame(D = dbh_seq))
) |>
  pivot_longer(-D, names_to = "Model", values_to = "H_pred")

ggplot(dat_fit, aes(x = D, y = H, color = plotId)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.4, size = 1.5) +
  geom_line(data = pred_df,
            aes(x = D, y = H_pred, linetype = Model),
            color = "black", linewidth = 1.2,
            inherit.aes = FALSE) +
  scale_color_manual(values = c(Plot1 = "#d73027", Plot2 = "#4575b4")) +
  scale_linetype_manual(values = c(Weibull = "solid", Michaelis_Menten = "dashed")) +
  labs(
    x = "DBH (cm)", y = "Height (m)",
    title = "H~D with Weibull and Michaelis-Menten fits",
    subtitle = "These are the two model forms used in BIOMASS::modelHD()",
    color = "Plot", linetype = "Model"
  )

kable(data.frame(
  Model = c("Weibull 3-parameter", "Michaelis-Menten"),
  Formula = c("H = a(1 \u2212 e^{\u2212b \u00b7 D^c})", "H = (a \u22c5 D) / (b + D)"),
  AIC = c(round(AIC(weib_fit), 1), round(AIC(mm_fit), 1)),
  RSE = c(round(summary(weib_fit)$sigma, 3), round(summary(mm_fit)$sigma, 3)),
  Note = c("Asymptotic with flexible curvature",
           "Asymptotic; simpler parameterisation"),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE
), caption = "Non-linear H~D model fit statistics (all plots combined)")
Non-linear H~D model fit statistics (all plots combined)

Weibull 3-parameter H = a(1 − e^{−b · D^c}) 5082.4 4.221 Asymptotic with flexible curvature
Michaelis-Menten H = (a ⋅ D) / (b + D) 5087.9 4.236 Asymptotic; simpler parameterisation

10 Use in BIOMASS AGB estimation

The NouraguesHD dataset is the default training data for BIOMASS::modelHD(), which fits local height-diameter models as an intermediate step in Chave et al. (2014) pantropical AGB estimation.

# Example workflow (not run — requires wood density lookup)
library(BIOMASS)

# 1. Fit a local H~D model using Nouragues data
hd_model <- modelHD(
  D      = NouraguesHD$D,
  H      = NouraguesHD$H,
  method = "weibull"   # or "michaelis", "log1", "log2", "log3"
)

# 2. Predict heights for your trees
H_pred <- predictHD(D = my_trees$DBH_cm, model = hd_model, plot = FALSE)

# 3. Get wood densities
wd <- getWoodDensity(genus = my_trees$genus, species = my_trees$species)

# 4. Compute AGB with Chave et al. 2014 eq. 4
AGB <- computeAGB(D = my_trees$DBH_cm, WD = wd$meanWD, H = H_pred$H,
                  coord = cbind(my_trees$long, my_trees$lat))

Caveat: Using Nouragues H-D to predict heights for forests outside French Guiana introduces systematic bias proportional to the difference in local H-D relationships. Local calibration data are preferred wherever available.

12 Notes for allometric merging

  1. DBH range is >= 10 cm — this is a canopy-tree dataset. It lacks saplings and small trees (< 10 cm DBH), which limits its use as a universal H~D calibration dataset.

  2. Only 2 plots, same reserve — all data come from one site (Nouragues). H-D relationships trained here may not transfer well to other tropical regions.

  3. 163 NAs in height — trees without height measurements must be imputed before using the Chave et al. (2014) AGB equation, which requires height as input.

  4. DBH units are cm — compatible with BAAD, Tallo, and NEON (no conversion needed).

  5. Taxonomy uses genus + species columns (not a single scientificName); concatenate them before merging with other sources.

  6. Coordinates are plot centroids, not individual tree positions.
